[[File:Crawling hand icon.png|left]]
'''Crawling hands''' are [[Slayer]] monsters that require level 5 Slayer to kill, and are the second [[Slayer monsters]] that beginning Slayers can kill, the first being [[gelatinous abomination]]s. They frequently drop gloves and rings, since they are reanimated severed hands. They are also one of the creatures that will sometimes "die" in a perfect form, dropping as a [[crawling hand (item)|crawling hand item]] that can be stuffed by a [[taxidermist]] and mounted in a [[player-owned house]]. The [[crawling hand (stuffed)|stuffed hand]] along with 5 zeal points can also be exchanged for a [[creeping hand]] [[Summoning pet]] at [[Soul Wars]].

Players can also kill [[skeletal hand]]s and [[zombie hand]]s as part of a [[Crawling hands (Slayer assignment)|crawling hand Slayer task]]. These monsters yield more slayer and combat experience than crawling hands and have better drops. Skeletal and zombie hands are found in the [[Meiyerditch Dungeon]], which can only be accessed during and after the [[Legacy of Seergaze]] [[quest]].

Crawling hands are susceptible to [[salve amulet]]s and other [[Undead slayer (effect)|undead slayer effects]]. Crawling hands can be fought on [[slayer contracts]], giving 9.6 and 11.3 experience on special contracts for the level 6 and level 10 versions, respectively.

Players can use a [[mask of Broken Fingers]] (or its helm variant [[Helm of the Dead Hand]]) to kill these, especially when on a slayer assignment, to take advantage of its benefits.

The crawling hands in the [[Burthorpe Slayer Cave]] are one of the few types of monsters that drop [[gold charm]]s in free-to-play.

==Trivia==
* The concept probably originated from the story, "La Main Gauche" from French author {{WP|Guy de Maupassant}}. This theory is backed up by the ability to display the hand in one's home, as in the story. Another possible origin might be the wallmasters/floormasters from the {{WP|The Legend of Zelda|The Legend of Zelda series}} or Thing from {{WP|The Addams Family}}. Another possible inspiration was from the B-movie {{WP|The Crawling Hand}}, in which an astronaut burns up and crash lands with his hand being the only surviving part, which becomes animated via radiation, or from {{WP|Dr. Terror's House of Horrors}}, in which the protagonist is haunted by the severed, crawling hand of his enemy who committed suicide.
* Their appearance was updated on [[5 June]] [[2008]].
*The black markings seen on some of the crawling hands is very similar to the appearance of Ash's possessed hand from ''{{WP|Evil Dead 2}}'', which he severs with a chainsaw, after which it crawls about on its own.
* All crawling hands seem to be right hands.
* Crawling hands are the lowest level monster that drop the [[Vecna skull]].
